subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: Which prominent national leader served as the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of India, playing the historic role of integrating over 500 princely states?
questions.explanation: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel served as Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Home and States, orchestrating the diplomatic integration of princely states into the Indian Union.

questions.question: In the first general elections of 1952, how many Lok Sabha seats were won by the Bharatiya Jana Sangh founded by Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee?
questions.explanation: The Bharatiya Jana Sangh won 3 seats in the first Lok Sabha in 1952, while the CPI emerged as the largest opposition party with 16 seats.

questions.question: The Green Revolution introduced in India in the mid-1960s was driven primarily by high-yielding varieties (HYV) of wheat originally developed in:
questions.explanation: High-yielding dwarf wheat varieties were developed by Dr. Norman Borlaug at CIMMYT in Mexico and adapted to Indian conditions by M.S. Swaminathan.

questions.question: Following his asylum in India in 1959, the Dalai Lama set up his spiritual headquarters and Tibetan government-in-exile at:
questions.explanation: Dharamshala (McLeod Ganj) in Himachal Pradesh was designated as the headquarters of the Central Tibetan Administration and residence of the Dalai Lama.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: The outcome of the fourth general elections of 1967, where Congress lost power in several states and saw its Lok Sabha majority slashed, was described by commentators as a:
questions.explanation: The 1967 election results were widely termed a 'political earthquake' because Congress lost assembly majorities across seven northern and eastern states.

questions.question: Who was the President of India who formally signed the proclamation of National Emergency on the night of 25 June 1975?
questions.explanation: President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed signed the Emergency proclamation on 25 June 1975 on the recommendation of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.

questions.question: The six-year mass agitation against illegal immigrants in Assam (1979-1985) was led primarily by the student organization named:
options: A) United Liberation Front of Asom (ULFA)
questions.explanation: The All Assam Students Union (AASU), along with the All Assam Gana Sangram Parishad (AAGSP), spearheaded the mass movement against illegal migrants.

questions.question: Which prominent environmental activists were at the forefront of the Chipko movement's tree-hugging protests in the Garhwal Himalayas?
options: A) Medha Patkar and Baba Amte
B) Mahendra Singh Tikait and Sharad Joshi
C) Aruna Roy and Nikhil Dey
D) Sunderlal Bahuguna and Chandi Prasad Bhatt
questions.explanation: Sunderlal Bahuguna and Chandi Prasad Bhatt provided inspirational leadership to the Chipko movement, spreading awareness of ecological conservation across the Himalayan valleys.

questions.question: In May 1998, India conducted a series of five underground nuclear tests (Pokhran-II) under the leadership of Prime Minister:
questions.explanation: The NDA government headed by Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee conducted the Pokhran-II tests (Operation Shakti) on 11 and 13 May 1998, declaring India a nuclear weapons state.

questions.question: Which nation was formally inducted into the BRIC group in 2010, converting it into the BRICS alliance?
questions.explanation: South Africa joined the grouping in December 2010 at the invitation of China, transforming BRIC into BRICS.

questions.question: In May 1960, the bilingual Bombay State was bifurcated into two separate linguistic states following sustained popular agitations:
questions.explanation: The Samyukta Maharashtra Samiti and Maha Gujarat Janata Parishad movements led to the Bombay Reorganisation Act of 1960, dividing Bombay into Maharashtra (Marathi) and Gujarat (Gujarati).

questions.question: The Congress Socialist Party (CSP) was formed within the Indian National Congress in 1934 by young socialist leaders including Jayaprakash Narayan, Ram Manohar Lohia, and:
questions.explanation: Acharya Narendra Deva was the founding president of the CSP in 1934, advocating socialist transformation of the Congress and Indian society.

questions.question: The Hirakud Dam, one of independent India's earliest multipurpose river valley projects, was constructed across which river in Odisha?
questions.explanation: The Hirakud Dam was built across the Mahanadi River in Sambalpur, Odisha, inaugurated in 1957 to control floods, generate hydroelectricity, and irrigate agricultural lands.

questions.question: The Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence (Panchsheel) were first formally articulated in the preamble to which bilateral agreement in April 1954?
options: A) Indo-Soviet Treaty of Peace and Friendship
B) Sino-Indian Agreement on Trade and Intercourse between the Tibet Region of China and India
C) Simla Agreement between India and Pakistan
D) Indo-Nepalese Treaty of Peace and Friendship
questions.explanation: Panchsheel was incorporated into the preamble of the bilateral trade agreement signed between India and China regarding the Tibet region on 29 April 1954.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Following India's decisive military victory in the 1971 Bangladesh Liberation War, Indira Gandhi's Congress (R) party swept which elections with landslide majorities?
options: C) The 1972 State Legislative Assembly elections
D) The 1975 Municipal elections in Delhi
questions.explanation: Capitalizing on national euphoria and Indira Gandhi's stature as a war leader, Congress (R) won massive majorities in nearly all state assemblies that went to polls in 1972.

questions.question: During the Emergency of 1975-1977, which Article of the Constitution was invoked by presidential order to suspend the right of citizens to move courts for the enforcement of fundamental rights?
questions.explanation: Under Article 359, the President issued orders suspending the right of citizens to move any court for the enforcement of rights guaranteed under Articles 14, 19, 21, and 22.

questions.question: On which date did Maharaja Hari Singh sign the Instrument of Accession to the Dominion of India following tribal incursions armed by Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession on 26 October 1947, requesting Indian military assistance to repel Pakistani raiders attacking the Kashmir valley.

questions.question: The grassroots agitation by the Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan (MKSS) demanding transparency in village development muster rolls originated in which district of Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: MKSS began its struggles for minimum wages and public audit of development records in Devdungri village and Kotkirana in Rajsamand district of Rajasthan.

questions.question: The Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), seeking to mobilize the Bahujan (Dalits, OBCs, and religious minorities) for political power, was founded in 1984 under the leadership of:
questions.explanation: Kanshi Ram established the BSP on 14 April 1984, building on previous socio-political organizations like BAMCEF and the Dalit Shoshit Samaj Sangharsh Samiti (DS4).

questions.question: Who serves as the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog under its institutional governance framework?
options: B) The Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog
D) The Prime Minister of India
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister of India is the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog, supported by a full-time Vice-Chairman, CEO, and Governing Council comprising all Chief Ministers.

questions.topic: Cold War Era and Non-aligned Movement
questions.question: During the Korean War (1950-1953), India played a crucial mediating role and chaired which international commission established to oversee the repatriation of prisoners of war?
options: B) United Nations Command Disarmament Committee
questions.explanation: India chaired the Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission (NNRC) headed by General K.S. Thimayya, successfully supervising the exchange of prisoners of war after the 1953 armistice.

questions.question: In Central Asia, which former Soviet republic witnessed a brutal ten-year civil war from 1992 to 2001 driven by clan rivalries and religious extremism?
questions.explanation: Tajikistan suffered a devastating civil war between government forces and the United Tajik Opposition from 1992 until a UN-sponsored peace agreement in 1997 with final stabilization around 2001.

questions.question: Which US President declared the emergence of a 'New World Order' following the decisive UN-authorized coalition victory in the First Gulf War in 1991?
questions.explanation: President George H.W. Bush proclaimed the dawn of a 'New World Order' based on American leadership, collective security, and international rule of law after Operation Desert Storm.

questions.question: The original five member states that signed the Bangkok Declaration in 1967 were Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, and:
questions.explanation: Thailand was the fifth founding member state along with Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, and Singapore that established ASEAN on 8 August 1967.

questions.question: In which year did the People's Republic of China formally become a member of the World Trade Organization (WTO), cementing its integration into the global economy?
questions.explanation: China joined the WTO on 11 December 2001 after 15 years of negotiations, accelerating its rise as the world's leading manufacturing and export powerhouse.

questions.question: In October 1999, which Pakistani military general led a bloodless coup d'état ousting the democratically elected government of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif?
questions.explanation: Army Chief General Pervez Musharraf overthrew Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif in a military coup on 12 October 1999, ruling as Chief Executive and later as President until 2008.

questions.sub_topic: Indian Peace Keeping Force in Sri Lanka
questions.question: In 1987, the Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF) was deployed to northern Sri Lanka to enforce peace under an accord signed between Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and President:
questions.explanation: The Indo-Sri Lanka Peace Accord was signed on 29 July 1987 in Colombo by Rajiv Gandhi and Sri Lankan President Junius Richard Jayewardene, leading to the deployment of the IPKF.

questions.question: The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO), which promotes international cooperation in education and heritage preservation, is headquartered in:
questions.explanation: UNESCO was established on 16 November 1945 and is headquartered in Paris, France.

questions.question: The International Court of Justice (ICJ), the principal judicial organ of the United Nations, adjudicates legal disputes between sovereign states from its seat at:
questions.explanation: The ICJ sits at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands, comprising 15 judges elected for nine-year terms by the UN General Assembly and Security Council.

questions.question: India refused to sign the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT) opened for signature in 1996 primarily on the grounds that:
options: A) It mandated an immediate war declaration against non-signatory nations
B) The treaty was discriminatory, allowing existing nuclear weapon states to maintain their arsenals and conduct sub-critical computer simulations
C) It prohibited civilian nuclear power plants across Asia
D) It excluded all Asian nations from membership in the United Nations
questions.explanation: India opposed the CTBT because it froze the nuclear monopoly of the P5 without establishing a binding time-bound roadmap for global nuclear disarmament.

questions.question: Agenda 21, adopted by consensus at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit, is best understood as:
options: A) A legally binding military protocol against deforestation in Antarctica
B) A mandatory 21-point penal code for maritime plastic pollution
C) A comprehensive non-binding blueprint of action for global sustainable development in the 21st century
D) A treaty establishing a single international carbon tax on all developing states
questions.explanation: Agenda 21 is a comprehensive plan of action adopted at UNCED 1992 to promote sustainable development, combating poverty and environmental degradation at local, national, and global levels.

questions.question: The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), which entered into force in 1994, established annual diplomatic negotiating sessions known as:
questions.explanation: The supreme decision-making body of the UNFCCC is the Conference of the Parties (COP), which meets annually to assess progress and negotiate climate treaties like the Kyoto Protocol and Paris Agreement.

questions.question: Critics of economic globalisation from the political Left contend that it primarily results in:
options: A) Reduction in state welfare capacity, privatization of public goods, and deepening economic disparities
B) Excessive expansion of socialist state enterprises and government subsidies
C) Total elimination of corporate profits and multinational investments
D) Universal military disarmament across all industrialized countries
questions.explanation: Left critics argue that neoliberal globalisation weakens the state's capacity to protect poor citizens, rolls back social safety nets, privatizes public utilities, and benefits corporate elites at the expense of working classes.

questions.question: In November 1947, the Government of India signed a Standstill Agreement with the Nizam of Hyderabad for a period of one year. What was the central objective of this agreement?
options: A) To grant Hyderabad complete international recognition as an independent sovereign member of the UN.
B) To maintain pre-independence administrative arrangements and buy time for negotiations while preventing immediate military conflict or external interference.
C) To permanently cede the coastal districts of Andhra to the Nizam's direct administrative sovereignty.
D) To transfer all military garrisons in Secunderabad permanently to the armed forces of Pakistan.
questions.explanation: The Standstill Agreement (November 1947) froze existing political relations for one year, allowing Sardar Patel and V.P. Menon to negotiate integration while preventing the Nizam from leasing ports to foreign powers.

questions.question: In July 1959, the Union Government invoked Article 356 of the Constitution to dismiss the first elected Communist ministry of Kerala led by E.M.S. Namboodiripad following:
options: A) A violent armed border invasion by Chinese paramilitary forces into Wayanad.
B) The unanimous refusal of the Kerala legislature to pass the annual state budget.
C) The 'Vimochana Samaram' (Liberation Struggle) spearheaded by Christian churches, the Nair Service Society, and the Congress party protesting the Education Bill.
D) A formal resolution by the Kerala High Court declaring all communist parties unlawful.
questions.explanation: The communist ministry's agrarian and education reforms provoked opposition from private school managers, church groups, and the NSS, leading to the Congress-backed 'Vimochana Samaram' and the controversial dismissal under Article 356.

questions.question: Chaudhary Charan Singh's influential critique of early Five Year Plans in works such as 'India's Economic Policy: Gandhian Blueprint' argued that:
options: A) Agricultural production should be entirely collectivized on Soviet-style Kolkhoz state farms.
B) India should dismantle all rural canals and rely exclusively on imported American foodgrains under PL-480.
C) All private landholdings should be merged into state-run industrial manufacturing complexes.
D) Heavy industrial planning extracted agrarian surpluses through adverse terms of trade to subsidize capital-intensive urban industries, breeding rural poverty and unemployment.
questions.explanation: Charan Singh argued that central planners favored heavy urban industry at the expense of agriculture, transferring capital from villages to cities and neglecting peasant smallholders.

questions.question: Which clandestine Chinese infrastructure project discovered by India in 1957 significantly aggravated Sino-Indian border tensions leading to the 1962 war?
options: A) The construction of a strategic military highway (China National Highway 219) through the Aksai Chin region linking Xinjiang and Tibet
B) The installation of a long-range radar station in the Chumbi Valley near Sikkim
C) The construction of a deep-water naval submarine base in the Gulf of Tonkin
D) The establishment of a military airstrip inside the Tawang monastery compound
questions.explanation: In 1957, China completed Highway 219 connecting Xinjiang with western Tibet through Aksai Chin (claimed by India as part of Ladakh), shocking Indian authorities when published on Chinese maps.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Following the 1967 electoral setbacks, the Congress Working Committee adopted the radical 'Ten-Point Programme' which prominently included:
options: A) Immediate privatization of all railways and post offices to private industrial trusts
B) Social control of banks, nationalization of general insurance, public distribution of foodgrains, and ceilings on urban property
C) Dismantling of the Planning Commission and abolition of all agricultural income exemptions
D) Compulsory military conscription for all university graduates
questions.explanation: In May 1967, the CWC adopted the Ten-Point Programme incorporating socialist policies: social control of banking institutions, nationalization of general insurance, state trading in foodgrains, and urban land ceilings.

questions.question: In the infamous ADM Jabalpur v. Shivkant Shukla (1976) case, also known as the Habeas Corpus case, the majority of the Supreme Court held that:
options: A) The proclamation of Emergency was unconstitutional and all detained political leaders must be immediately released.
B) The Union Cabinet had no legal authority to enact censorship on newspapers.
C) Under the presidential order suspending fundamental rights during Emergency, no person could move a court for habeas corpus even against illegal or mala fide detentions.
D) Detainees retained the inviolable right to personal liberty under natural law that could never be suspended.
questions.explanation: A 4:1 majority held that during Emergency, citizens could not approach the courts to protect life and personal liberty under Article 21, with Justice H.R. Khanna famously delivering the lone heroic dissent.

questions.question: How did Operation Black Thunder II (May 1988) in the Golden Temple differ crucially from Operation Blue Star (June 1984) in its tactical execution and public perception?
options: A) It deployed heavy naval aviation and aerial chemical dispersants over Amritsar.
B) It imposed total censorship and destroyed the Akal Takht for the second time.
C) It was led by international peacekeeping forces mandated by the UN Security Council.
D) It was executed by the National Security Guard (NSG) and Punjab Police with minimal holy sanctum damage, full media coverage, and zero tank artillery, resulting in mass terrorist surrenders.
questions.explanation: Operation Black Thunder II utilized NSG commandos and Punjab Police snipers under K.P.S. Gill, surrounded the temple without entering the sanctum sanctorum, allowed full media coverage, cut water/electricity, and forced militants to surrender openly.

questions.question: The Anti-Arrack Movement in Andhra Pradesh was distinct from conventional trade union protests because it framed alcoholism primarily as:
options: A) A direct structural cause of domestic violence against women, indebtedness, and household pauperization sponsored by the state-contractor nexus for excise revenue.
B) A religious blasphemy punishable by public excommunication under caste councils.
C) An ideological violation of orthodox Marxist agrarian dialectics.
D) A technical municipal violation regarding the licensing of commercial liquor bottling plants.
questions.explanation: The rural women of Nellore exposed how arrack drained daily wages, precipitated physical abuse of wives and children, and enriched politicians and arrack contractors while impoverishing families.

questions.sub_topic: Rise of Regional Backward Caste Parties
questions.question: The political realignments of the early 1990s in north India resulted in the fragmentation of the Janata Dal into powerful regional parties asserting backward-caste empowerment. Which of the following correctly pairs these parties with their founders?
options: A) Samajwadi Party — Nitish Kumar; Rashtriya Janata Dal — Ram Vilas Paswan
B) Samajwadi Party — Mulayam Singh Yadav; Rashtriya Janata Dal — Lalu Prasad Yadav
C) Bahujan Samaj Party — Lalu Prasad Yadav; Janata Dal (United) — Kanshi Ram
D) Lok Janshakti Party — Mulayam Singh Yadav; Biju Janata Dal — Sharad Yadav
questions.explanation: Mulayam Singh Yadav founded the Samajwadi Party in October 1992, and Lalu Prasad Yadav founded the Rashtriya Janata Dal in July 1997, both building powerful OBC-minority electoral coalitions.

questions.topic: Cold War Era and Non-aligned Movement
questions.question: The UN General Assembly's 1974 Declaration on the Establishment of a New International Economic Order (NIEO) was primarily designed to:
options: A) Abolish all national currencies in favor of the US gold standard.
B) Impose universal trade tariffs on all agricultural exports from the Global South.
C) Give developing nations sovereignty over their natural resources, fairer terms of trade, and access to Western technology and markets.
D) Transfer all multinational private enterprises to direct Soviet command planning.
questions.explanation: NIEO sought to revise the international economic system in favor of Third World countries, granting control over natural resources, reducing trade deficits, and democratizing international financial institutions.

questions.question: Under Russia's Shock Therapy program in 1992-1994, the mass privatization of state assets through privatization vouchers resulted in:
options: A) The equitable distribution of corporate wealth to every Russian household, eliminating poverty overnight.
B) The permanent nationalization of all banking institutions under the Russian Orthodox Church.
C) The complete replacement of Russian industries with state-owned enterprises from China.
D) The 'largest garage sale in history', where valuable industrial enterprises were acquired at throwaway prices by emerging oligarchs while ordinary citizens sold vouchers for food.
questions.explanation: Voucher privatization collapsed into corruption and fire sales: nearly 70% of state enterprises were acquired by wealthy insiders and mafia oligarchs for a fraction of their worth, impoverishing the public.

questions.question: The First Gulf War (1991) was frequently termed a 'computer war' or 'video game war' because:
options: A) The US military deployed widespread laser-guided smart bombs, global positioning satellite networks, and live television broadcasts, highlighting an enormous technological gulf with other nations.
B) It was fought entirely in simulated digital software environments without any actual physical combat or casualties.
C) The Iraqi military successfully disabled US command centers using early internet cyber warfare.
D) Both sides agreed to settle boundary disputes through automated artificial intelligence arbitrations.
questions.explanation: Desert Storm demonstrated American precision-guided weapons, electronic warfare, and satellite communications broadcast live 24/7 on CNN, demonstrating qualitative technological superiority.

questions.question: The Treaty of Lisbon, which entered into force in December 2009 to streamline the constitutional functioning of the enlarged European Union, established:
options: A) A single unified military force replacing the national armies of all EU member states.
B) A permanent President of the European Council and a High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy.
C) The complete abolition of all national parliaments across Europe.
D) A compulsory European nuclear weapons arsenal controlled by the European Court of Justice.
questions.explanation: The Lisbon Treaty replaced the six-month rotating presidency with a permanent European Council President and strengthened EU external representation through the High Representative.

questions.question: The landmark 1996 Ganga Water Sharing Treaty signed between Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda of India and Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina of Bangladesh resolved the allocation of dry-season waters at the:
options: A) Teesta Barrage for a duration of 10 years
B) Tipaimukh Dam for a duration of 50 years
C) Farakka Barrage for a duration of 30 years
D) Hardinge Bridge for a duration of 15 years
questions.explanation: Signed on 12 December 1996, the historic treaty guaranteed sharing of the Ganga waters at Farakka Barrage in West Bengal during the lean season (January to May) for 30 years.

questions.question: The United Nations Trusteeship Council, one of the principal organs of the UN, officially suspended its operations in November 1994 following the independence of:
options: D) Palau, the last remaining UN Trust Territory
questions.explanation: The Trusteeship Council completed its mandate and suspended operations on 1 November 1994 when Palau, the last trust territory administered by the United States, gained independence.

questions.question: In contemporary security studies, Confidence-Building Measures (CBMs) differ from formal arms control disarmament treaties in that CBMs primarily aim to:
options: A) Mandate the unilateral destruction of all offensive conventional weapons within six months.
B) Prevent accidental conflict and miscalculation through regular communication, transparency of military exercises, and hotlines, without necessarily reducing weapons stockpiles.
C) Transfer command of national border defense forces to the UN Peacekeeping Department.
D) Impose automatic economic boycotts against any nation expanding its defense budget.
questions.explanation: CBMs are risk-reduction mechanisms (e.g., prior notification of military exercises, hotlines, exchange of observers) designed to avoid accidental escalations by improving transparency rather than eliminating weapons.

questions.question: The 1979 Agreement Governing the Activities of States on the Moon and Other Celestial Bodies (the Moon Agreement) declared that:
options: A) Only spacefaring superpowers holding confirmed lunar landings hold commercial mining franchises on the Moon.
B) Nuclear missile silos may be established on the far side of the Moon for international planetary defense.
C) The Moon is subject to the maritime territorial jurisdiction of the United Nations Security Council.
D) The Moon and its natural resources are the common heritage of mankind, prohibiting any state from claiming national sovereignty or private ownership over any part of it.
questions.explanation: Article 11 of the 1979 Moon Agreement designates the Moon and celestial bodies as the 'common heritage of mankind', forbidding national appropriation and requiring an equitable international regime to govern resource exploitation.
